reading.rtitle: The night I lost my voice
paras: I had waited eight months for that night. The tickets had sold out in ten minutes, and my cousin had stayed up until midnight to get them. So when we got stuck in traffic on the way to the stadium, I almost cried. By the time we arrived, the opening act had already finished, and the crowd had started singing on their own.

Then the lights went off. I had seen him on my phone a thousand times, but I had never seen him live, and it was completely different. He changed the setlist and started with a song nobody expected. I lost my voice in the third song. My cousin had lost hers before we even sat down.

That was a year ago. Since then, I have been to two more shows, and I have kept every wristband. But I have never felt anything like that first night. Next year the line-up is even bigger. I have not bought my ticket yet. This time I will not wait until midnight.

gist.prompt: What is the blog really about?
choices: How to buy tickets for a show that sells out.
A first concert that she still remembers as the best one.
Why going to shows with a cousin is a bad idea.

items: “my cousin had stayed up until midnight to get them.” Her cousin got them.
“By the time we arrived, the opening act had already finished.”
Ruby had seen the singer live before that night.
“I had never seen him live.” She had only seen him on her phone.
Ruby has already bought a ticket for next year.
